findings.title: Public `findMany` method removed without migrating callers
findings.body: `InsightsBookingService.findMany(findManyArgs)` was replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. The return types of `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` also changed from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`. Only the service and its test are modified in this PR. Any existing caller (for example the insights tRPC handlers) that calls `findMany`, or spreads these conditions into a Prisma `where`, will fail to compile. A raw `Sql` object passed into a `where` clause would be invalid. Please verify no other usages exist, or update them to use `$queryRaw` with `getBaseConditions()`.

findings.title: Loosened constructor type lets invalid team scope compile and silently return no data
findings.body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope, instead of the discriminated union. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and it type-checks. The zod `safeParse` then fails, so `this.options` becomes null and the service returns `1=0`. That caller gets an empty result set with no error, and the mistake can no longer be caught at compile time.

findings.title: Org-scope assertion depends on unordered DB result order
findings.body: The test compares the generated SQL, including array parameter values, with exact ordering: team IDs `[org, team, team2, team3]` and user IDs `[user, user2, user3]`. Those arrays come from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds` queries that have no ORDER BY. Postgres does not guarantee row order without one, so the test can fail intermittently even though the authorization logic is correct.

findings.title: Caching tests removed and SQL execution only covered for user scope
findings.body: The caching tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` were deleted, although the caching logic still exists in the service. The only test that runs the generated SQL against the database uses user scope. The org and team scope SQL, which is the security-sensitive part and uses `= ANY(array)` parameter binding, is only compared structurally and never executed. A SQL syntax or type error in those paths would not be caught by these tests.
